source.title: Poisoned at Scale: A Scalable Audit Uncovers Hidden Scam Endpoints in Production LLMs
source.authors: Zhi-Yang Chen; Tara Saba; Xun Deng; Xujie Si; Fan Long

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. It includes appendix material; no apparent truncation affects this record.
record.tranche_reason: The study audits malicious URL generation in code, not held-out cross-entropy, loss extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, or downstream task performance. Its Gemma-3 size comparison measures a different outcome and does not test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The study reports extensive malicious-code rates, guardrail results, and retrieval-augmented results, but these do not measure the scaling-law claims. The Gemma-3 size-ablation results are recorded as a related finding with versions ["none"], not as evidence about loss scaling.
record.test_reason: The study audits how often production LLMs emit malicious URLs in generated code. It measures no pretraining loss, no fits, no compute allocation, no architecture shape and no downstream capability scaling. The Gemma-3 4b/12b/27b size ablation reports malicious-URL rates only, a safety behaviour rather than task performance, so it bears on no version. Scaling laws are not tested or cited as a method; the record's 'discusses' overstates the link. The paper mentions large training-data scale only in passing, so the closest category is cites_only/T6.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors conclude that malicious URL generation persists across Gemma-3 sizes (34.86%–41.61%). They read the 4b model's lower rate as plausibly reflecting weaker capability and shallower task fulfilment (shorter outputs, fewer URLs), not clearly stronger safety. The 12b and 27b models show similarly high rates.
record.recipe_differences: No scaling-law fitting or loss-measurement recipe is used.
record.method_sensitivity: For the related malicious-code outcome, rates vary with model size and prompt category. The study also reports variation across model/provider, sampling temperature, prompt pattern, and retrieval conditions; none of these tests concerns loss scaling.

fits_no_version.finding: Across Gemma-3 4b/12b/27b instruct models, the overall malicious-URL rate was 34.86%, 41.61% and 41.18% (Table 12). The authors attribute the lower 4b rate partly to shorter outputs and fewer URLs emitted.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The rate of malicious-endpoint generation on Innoc2Scam-bench rises from 4b to 12b in Gemma-3, then plateaus. This is a safety behaviour, not loss or capability scaling.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The study does not measure any loss-scaling claim. The Gemma-3 size-ablation rates have no confidence intervals stated in the reported table and cover only three models from one family on a targeted stress-test benchmark.
record.rows_left_out: No results were omitted. Other reported malicious-code, guardrail, and retrieval results do not measure the claim versions and are not recorded as rows.

untested.parts: No held-out loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
No shape or architecture comparison at fixed parameter count.
No power-law tests in other modalities or regimes.
No downstream task performance against scale or loss. Malicious-URL rate is a safety outcome.

record.verdict_notes: Off-topic for scaling laws. The relation should be cites_only rather than discusses: the paper does not discuss scaling laws. Table 3 parameter counts are model specifications, not results.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fits or comparison of predicted and observed loss on larger runs.
No compute-budget sweep or loss-minimizing parameter/token allocation.
No architecture comparison measuring loss at fixed parameter count.
No power-law loss tests in other modalities or training regimes.
No downstream task performance tested against scale or pretraining loss; malicious-code generation is a different outcome.
No fitting choices, exponents, or loss-curve departures are evaluated.
